note: The two sets are nearly identical in content: both capture the s-coordinate endpoints, the composite layer definition, the IEA ontology standard, the flatback trailing-edge definition, and the three damping values, and both make the same errors. Both misread the first edgewise damping as 5% (the page states 3%, 3%, 6%) and alter the quote accordingly, and both add a garbled, misbound flatback claim on top of the correct trailing-edge claim. Both also carry the same duplicated s-coordinate claims and the same trivial figure-label claims (Plane of Rotation, Chord Line, Pitch Axis, Arc Width, Offset, theta_rot). The only differences are cosmetic (theta_rot vs θrot, and the wording of the redundant flatback claim), so the sets are effectively equivalent.
remarks: Both sets misread the damping sentence: the page says 3%, 3%, and 6% for flapwise, edgewise, and torsional modes; the edgewise value is 3%, not 5%, and both quotes were altered to '3%, 5%, and 6%'. Both also duplicate the s-coordinate endpoint facts under two entity names and include a garbled flatback claim ('For flat ge is deﬁned as the midpoint...') that is redundant with the correct trailing-edge claim. Important facts both sets miss: the beam structural properties were computed with PreComp and VABS (NREL tool chain) or BECAS (DTU tool chain), producing stiffness matrices per cross section used in OpenFAST or HAWC2. The text layer garbles 'zero' as 'ero' and truncates the flatback sentence; the figure label is Θ_rot.
